items.note: The chips of ds-autocomplete and ds-multi-select now render inside a <span class="chip-row"> instead of sitting directly in the trigger. LAYOUT IS UNCHANGED: outside the new fit mode the wrapper is display:contents, so it adds no box and the chips remain flex items of the trigger exactly as before — spacing, wrapping and height are identical, and nothing needs doing if you never styled the chips from outside. WHAT BREAKS is a CSS override that walks the structure: any selector using the direct-child combinator from the trigger to a chip (`.autocomplete-trigger > ds-tag`, `ds-multi-select .trigger > ds-tag`, and `:first-child`/`:last-child`/`:nth-child` written against the trigger's children) now matches nothing or matches the wrapper. ACTION: drop the combinator (`.autocomplete-trigger ds-tag`) or insert `.chip-row`. Positional selectors should target `.chip-row > ds-tag:first-child` — note the chips are no longer siblings of the filter input, the addon slots or the chevron, so `ds-tag + .autocomplete-input` style adjacency is gone with no replacement. Chips also carry a `data-chip` attribute and the '+N more' marker a `data-chip-overflow` attribute; both are how the width measurement finds them, so do not strip them, but they are fine to select on.

This release's class-member-collision entry, the counterpart of 0.8.0's and 0.9.0's: it covers every exported class whose member surface changed, so a consumer who EXTENDS a DS component resolves them in one pass. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported (design-system.md), but where it happens the names collide and the build stops: TS4114 demands `override`, TS2415 fires on a redeclared private. WHAT GAINED MEMBERS: AutocompleteComponent and MultiSelectComponent each gained `fitsChipsToWidth`, `chipRow` and `chipsThatFit` — the three fields behind maxVisibleChips="fit". No member was removed and no signature changed. ACTION: rename the subclass's own member, or add `override` if the base's semantics genuinely match. Consumers who only use the <ds-...> elements in templates need no change.

informational: ds-autocomplete and ds-multi-select accept maxVisibleChips="fit" — the chips are capped by MEASURED width rather than a count, so one line holds as many as the trigger is wide and the rest collapse into '+N more', re-split whenever the trigger resizes. Purely additive and opt-in: the input still takes a number and still defaults to null (show everything), and nothing changes for a picker that does not ask for it. Choose by what has to stay predictable — a number pins the trigger's HEIGHT whatever the width, 'fit' pins the width and lets the count move.

The measurement behind maxVisibleChips="fit" runs ONLY when that mode is on: a picker on the default does not observe, measure or force layout, so adopting the release costs nothing on pages full of pickers that keep wrapping.

DELETE-LIST: if you wrote a ResizeObserver, a container query or a hand-tuned per-breakpoint maxVisibleChips number to keep a chip trigger on one line -> maxVisibleChips="fit" replaces it, and it re-splits on any width change rather than at the breakpoints you listed.

DELETE-LIST: if you capped a chip trigger's height with max-height plus overflow:hidden to stop it growing a line per selection -> that clips a chip mid-glyph and hides the count; maxVisibleChips (a number, or "fit") drops whole chips and reports how many are hidden.
